stories.headline: OpenAI releases 722 math papers in 372 result families from an unreleased internal model

key_facts.fact: On October 6, 2026 OpenAI released a broad range of new mathematical results produced by an internal frontier model, saying it consulted the independent Advisory Group on Mathematics and AI at the Institute for Advanced Study.
key_facts.excerpt: We're releasing a broad range of new mathematical results produced by an internal frontier model. We've been consulting with the independent Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence at the Institute for Advanced Study

key_facts.fact: The release comprises 722 manuscripts grouped into 372 result families, published in a GitHub repository; the model was given about 4,000 problems.
key_facts.excerpt: The Sam Altman-led AI startup has released 722 manuscripts spanning 372 groups of results ... the internal frontier model was given about 4,000 mathematical problems

key_facts.fact: OpenAI says the average result used compute equivalent to roughly three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking, and it published 10 summaries of the model's reasoning.
key_facts.excerpt: These include 10 summaries of the model's reasoning, estimations of compute spent in terms of Pro usage on ChatGPT, and statistics about the number of attempted problems. The average result used the equivalent compute of roughly three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking.

key_facts.fact: Claimed results include a solution to the four-dimensional Kakeya conjecture and progress toward the Riemann hypothesis; many results are verified in the Lean proof language.
key_facts.excerpt: Among the results claimed are a solution to the four-dimensional Kakeya conjecture, improvements on some of the world's most important computer algorithms and actual progress toward math's scariest problem, the Riemann hypothesis.

key_facts.fact: An OpenAI spokesperson said the unreleased model produced almost every result from a single prompt to a single AI agent, unlike the 10,000-agent swarm used for its earlier Navier-Stokes claim.
key_facts.excerpt: produced almost every one of the results in response to a single prompt handed to a single AI agent. This would be a striking difference from OpenAI's earlier blockbuster solution to the Navier-Stokes problem, which was produced through the collective efforts of a 10,000-strong agentic swarm

key_facts.fact: OpenAI did not publish prompts or per-result compute as the advisory group recommended, saying it is not bound by the recommendations; it says it is working to release the model.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI is choosing only to reveal the average compute time for a problem, with some additional statistics—and no prompts. The OpenAI spokesperson told Scientific American that the team is taking the advisory group's guidelines seriously ... but added that the company is not bound by these recommendations.

key_facts.fact: Family 003 claims no Dirichlet L-function, including the Riemann zeta function, has a zero with real part above 7/8 (a 'quasi-Riemann hypothesis'); the repository lists 162 papers with a formalized main result.
key_facts.excerpt: No Dirichlet L-function, the Riemann zeta function included, has a zero with real part above 7/8, which the entry calls the quasi-Riemann hypothesis ... the repository's catalogue lists 162 papers with a formalized main result.

key_facts.fact: Sam Altman reacted to the release by writing 'We are entering a new era of discovery now.'
key_facts.excerpt: We are entering a new era of discovery now

stories.headline: Mistral previews Large 4 'Le Chonk', a 1T-parameter model with open weights due October 27

key_facts.fact: Mistral AI launched a public preview of Mistral Large 4 (ML4), a natively multimodal model with 1 trillion parameters and 49 billion active, available via preview API on Mistral Studio.
key_facts.excerpt: Mistral AI has launched a public preview of Mistral Large 4 (ML4), a natively multimodal model with 1 trillion parameters and 49 billion active parameters, available through a preview API on Mistral Studio.

key_facts.fact: ML4 was trained from scratch on 3,800 Nvidia Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral's own European datacenters.
key_facts.excerpt: The company said ML4 was trained from scratch on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in its own European datacenters.

key_facts.fact: Mistral says weights will be released on October 27, after red-teaming with cybersecurity leaders, vetted partners and state authorities; it calls it the most powerful open-weight system outside China.
key_facts.excerpt: Mistral has released a preview of Mistral Large 4, a 1T model that the Paris-based company says is the most powerful open-weight AI system outside China ... The model weights ... will be available on October 27.

key_facts.fact: Documentation lists 1.05 trillion total parameters, a one-million-token context window, and pricing of $0.68 per million input tokens and $2.09 per million output tokens.
key_facts.excerpt: 1.05 trillion total parameters, 49 billion active parameters, and a 1.6-billion-parameter vision encoder, alongside a one-million-token context window ... pricing of $0.68 per million input tokens, $0.07 per million cached input tokens, and $2.09 per million output tokens.

key_facts.fact: Mistral says ML4 is competitive with the strongest open-source models globally while significantly outperforming any open-weight model developed in the US or Europe, and is state-of-the-art among open models on cybersecurity, finance and law.
key_facts.excerpt: It already achieves performance competitive with the strongest open-source models globally, while significantly outperforming any open-weight model developed in the US or Europe. On critical enterprise workloads, including cybersecurity, finance and law, we find it to be state-of-the-art among open models.

stories.headline: Anthropic merges Glasswing into a 3-tier cyber program opening Mythos 5.1 to vetted defenders

key_facts.fact: Anthropic launched an expanded Cyber Verification Program with three access tiers, each including Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Mythos 5.1 and future models.
key_facts.excerpt: The program now consists of three access tiers ... Each tier includes access to our most capable models, including Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Mythos 5.1, and new models moving forward.

key_facts.fact: The revamp integrates the CVP and Project Glasswing, which previously gave organizations securing critical software access to Mythos, into a single offering.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic on Tuesday announced a revamped Cyber Verification Program (CVP), integrating the CVP and Project Glasswing into a single offering, with three levels of access to its most capable AI models.

key_facts.fact: Tiers are Defense Access, Red Team Access (adds authorized penetration testing) and Specialized Access for testing systems like power grids, flight systems and interbank transfer infrastructure, vetted with the US government.
key_facts.excerpt: Specialized Access has the fewest cybersecurity blocks and is reserved for a limited group of verified organizations authorized to test high-risk systems ... The company reviews each applicant in collaboration with the US government.

key_facts.fact: On the CyScenarioBench evaluation, Opus 5.5 was blocked on every task without CVP; in Red Team Access it completed 34 of 50 tasks, roughly its 67.6% unsafeguarded success rate.
key_facts.excerpt: Without CVP access, every task was blocked on the first prompt ... In the Red Team Access tier, no blocks occurred, and Claude Opus 5.5 successfully completed 34 of the 50 tasks—effectively equivalent to the model's 67.6% success rate on this evaluation with no safeguards applied

key_facts.fact: Program members must accept data retention so Anthropic can monitor misuse until 'Enterprise Frontier Safeguards' arrives later this fall.
key_facts.excerpt: Data retention is required for organizations enrolled in ... program so that we can monitor for cyber misuse. Once Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS) ... is available later this fall, eligible organizations will be able to store data in cloud infrastructure they control.

key_facts.fact: The change comes a week after Anthropic warned about the cyber capabilities of Z.ai's open GLM-5.3 model.
key_facts.excerpt: Only a week after warning about the perils of competitor Z.ai's GLM-5.3 model and its advanced cybersecurity capabilities, Anthropic has expanded its Cyber Verification Program (CVP) – or rather, reconfigured it.

key_facts.excerpt: Nous Research has raised $90 million at a $1.5 billion valuation to bring open-source artificial intelligence assistants to business users.

stories.headline: Meta and Sierra launch Personal Agent Protocol with Walmart, Shopify, Stripe for agent-business links

key_facts.fact: Sierra's Bret Taylor and Clay Bavor announced Personal Agent Protocol, an open standard Meta and Sierra are developing with Genesys, Instinct, Rocket, Shopify, Stripe and Walmart.
key_facts.excerpt: Personal Agent Protocol — an open standard Meta and Sierra are developing along with industry partners at Genesys, Instinct, Rocket, Shopify, Stripe, and Walmart that defines how personal agents interact with businesses.

key_facts.fact: The protocol is designed to handle authentication and give companies visibility into what personal agents do through their websites, APIs or company agents.
key_facts.excerpt: We're designing it to handle authentication, empower consumers and give companies visibility into what personal agents do through their websites, APIs or company agents. It's open for anyone to implement.

key_facts.fact: It is built on OAuth with guest, read-only and write access tiers; a v0.1 spec and reference implementation are planned for later in October, with payments a future extension.
key_facts.excerpt: 3 access tiers: guest session, user-granted read-only, user-granted write ... v0.1 spec, design workshops and a reference implementation planned for October 2026; payments, finer permissions and push notifications are future extensions

key_facts.fact: Stripe and Shopify are also members of Visa's rival Trusted Agent Protocol.
key_facts.excerpt: Stripe and Shopify are among the partners. Both have already joined a rival protocol run by Visa.

key_facts.fact: The effort is meant to let agents like Meta's Muse, launched a month earlier, work with businesses.
key_facts.excerpt: Personal Agent Protocol is designed to enable agents like Meta's Muse work with businesses to get things done.

stories.headline: Common Sense Media rates ChatGPT for Teens an 'unacceptable risk'; OpenAI disputes the tests

key_facts.fact: Common Sense Media said OpenAI's ChatGPT for Teens, introduced in August, is an 'unacceptable risk' whose protections 'fall short of what the company promised.'
key_facts.excerpt: ChatGPT for Teens, introduced in August, has guardrails for teens ... Common Sense Media says that the teen protections offered by the feature "fall short of what the company promised."

key_facts.fact: The assessment found ChatGPT doesn't send parent alerts when it should, doesn't offer the right help in crises, and still does kids' homework.
key_facts.excerpt: ChatGPT "doesn't send alerts to parents when it should," doesn't offer "the right help in crisis situations," and "still does kids' homework"

key_facts.fact: Tom Siegel of Common Sense's Youth AI Safety Institute said a teen can talk about self-harm for an hour without a parent alert and that ChatGPT should be adults-only until fixed.
key_facts.excerpt: "A teen can spend an hour talking about self-harm without their parent getting a single alert. Until OpenAI fixes that and proves it with independent testing, ChatGPT should be for adults only."

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said the testing may have begun and ended before parental controls had finished activating, making findings inaccurate; Common Sense said it stands by its methodology.
key_facts.excerpt: Our review of Common Sense Media's methodology shows that the bulk of their testing may have begun and concluded before activation of parental controls was complete ... We stand behind our testing methodology and our results.

stories.headline: Musk says SpaceX and Tesla will run Terafab; TSMC at most a sublessee, Intel stays in

key_facts.fact: On October 7 Musk replied on X to a post saying TSMC would likely own and run the fab: "No, we will build and run the fab. Let there be ZERO doubt about that. Maybe TSMC subleases part of the Terafab if they want, but nothing more than that."
key_facts.excerpt: No, we will build and run the fab. Let there be ZERO doubt about that. Maybe TSMC subleases part of the Terafab if they want, but nothing more than that.

key_facts.fact: The clarification followed Musk's confirmation days earlier of talks with TSMC, after the Culpium newsletter reported TSMC was exploring ways to work with Terafab, most likely by owning and operating the new factory.
key_facts.excerpt: Last week, Musk said that there had been discussions about potential cooperation with TSMC on the Terafab project, without giving further details.

key_facts.fact: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan told Bloomberg in Tokyo on October 7, ahead of Intel's 50th-anniversary event in Japan, that Intel will remain involved in Terafab.
key_facts.excerpt: Tan said Intel would continue its participation in Terafab in an interview with Bloomberg in Tokyo on the 7th, ahead of an event marking the 50th anniversary of Intel's entry into Japan.

key_facts.fact: Intel shares fell 2.65% on October 5 and another 3.2% on October 6 on the TSMC talk, while TSMC closed at a record $485.80.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel fell 2.65% the previous day and another 3.2% on the 6th, a 5.7% drop over two sessions. TSMC rose 2.7% to a record close of $485.80 a share.

key_facts.fact: Terafab, in Grimes County, Texas, requires $16.8B in its first phase and up to $119B across all phases; Intel agreed in April to supply its 14A process, and first products are due in mid-2028.
key_facts.excerpt: requiring $16.8 billion ... in the first phase alone and up to $119 billion across all phases ... agreed in April to supply 14A process technology to the Terafab project ... Terafab's first products are due in mid-2028.

stories.headline: Micron's Taoyuan union in Taiwan wins strike mandate over bonus dispute

key_facts.fact: The union at Micron's Taoyuan operations said on October 7 it secured legal authorization to strike: of 2,258 eligible members, 2,012 voted, 1,994 in favor and 14 against (99% of votes cast, 88.3% of eligible members).
key_facts.excerpt: Of 2,258 eligible union members, 2,012 voted over the past six days, with 1,994 supporting strike action, 14 opposed and four invalid ballots. The result meant 88.3 percent of all eligible members backed a strike, or 99 percent of those who voted.

key_facts.fact: No strike date is set; union chairman Jerry Lin said a 'surprise strike' called by text message is an option, and the union wants a concrete proposal after Micron's October 8-9 board meeting.
key_facts.excerpt: The union said it hoped Micron's board would offer concrete proposals after a meeting scheduled for Oct. 8-9 U.S. time, before further action is taken.

key_facts.fact: Unions seek a one-off bonus of 83 months' salary and a permanent system allocating 15% of operating profit to quarterly bonuses; workers rejected Micron's September offer of up to 68 months of pay.
key_facts.excerpt: Workers want an 83-month one-off bonus and a permanent system giving 15% of operating profits to bonuses, with Micron's offer of up to 68 months rejected.

key_facts.fact: Micron makes around 50% to 60% of its chips in Taiwan, where two unions represent nearly 12,000 of its 15,000 workers at Taoyuan and Taichung.
key_facts.excerpt: Micron, which makes around 50% to 60% of its chips in Taiwan, has been locked in talks over remuneration with two labour unions representing nearly 12,000 of 15,000 workers

key_facts.fact: Micron shares traded about 2.6% lower in pre-market on October 7 after the vote.
key_facts.excerpt: Micron Technology shares traded roughly 2.6% lower in pre-market on Wednesday after a Taiwan union representing the company's workers secured authorization from its members to strike

key_facts.fact: Taiwan's Ministry of Labor urged Micron to put forward 'concrete, feasible proposals'; Micron said it would keep talking with the unions in good faith.
key_facts.excerpt: The ministry urged Micron to carefully consider workers' views and put forward "concrete, feasible proposals" for negotiations.

stories.headline: Finland orders Google to halt work on two data centers over forest clearing

key_facts.fact: On October 6 Finland's Licensing and Supervision Agency (LVV) ordered Google subsidiary Tuike Finland Oy to suspend environment-altering preparatory work at its planned data centers in Muhos and Kajaani by October 23, until environmental impact assessments are completed.
key_facts.excerpt: Finnish Licensing and Supervision Agency (LVV) on Tuesday issued a notice to Google subsidiary, Tuike Finland Oy, to suspend building work for data center projects planned for Muhos and Kajaani until the environmental impact assessments have been completed.

key_facts.fact: Tuike Finland had felled about 330 hectares of forest in Muhos without completing an environmental impact assessment, and reportedly logged just under 200 hectares in Kajaani.
key_facts.excerpt: Tuike Finland Oy, the company representing Google, had felled 330-hectares (815 acres) of forest in Muhos without completing an environmental impact assessment. In Kajaani, the company has reportedly been logging across just under 200 hectares

key_facts.fact: The company must respond in writing by October 14 or face possible enforcement proceedings.
key_facts.excerpt: Tuike Finland ... has been asked to provide an explanation and set out how it intends to proceed by 14 October. The agency said it could begin "enforcement proceedings" if the company failed to comply

key_facts.fact: Google said it had 'fallen short of our own high standards in this instance' and would follow the agency's guidance, including tree planting across 130 hectares at Muhos.
key_facts.excerpt: "We understand the concerns and have fallen short of our own high standards in this instance," a Google spokesperson told CNBC, adding that they would follow the LVV's guidance.

key_facts.fact: The order comes a month after Google committed to invest at least EUR 13B (about $15B) in Finland over 2027-2028, including new data centers in Kajaani, Muhos and Vaala.
key_facts.excerpt: Google announced last month that it would invest at least €13bn (£11bn; $15bn) in Finland over 2027 and 2028. Its plans included new data centres in Kajaani, Muhos and Vaala

stories.headline: Black Hills signs deal to power Google's Cheyenne data center with 2.7 GW resource mix

key_facts.fact: Black Hills Corp. announced on October 6 definitive agreements, with terms through 2048, to serve a planned Google data center in Cheyenne, Wyoming.
key_facts.excerpt: Black Hills Corp. (NYSE: BKH) today announced it has signed definitive agreements effective Sept. 30, 2026, with terms through 2048, to serve a planned Google data center to be constructed in Cheyenne, Wyoming.

key_facts.fact: The project will be served by a 2.7 GW resource mix: up to 590 MW of grid-connected service from Black Hills plus about 2.1 GW of third-party Wyoming resources managed through a private microgrid.
key_facts.excerpt: Black Hills will provide up to 590 MW of grid-connected energy service through company-owned generation and market energy. In addition, Black Hills will manage the output of approximately 2.1 GW of Wyoming-based, third-party contracted resources through a privately managed microgrid

key_facts.fact: Black Hills plans to invest $1.8B in 2027-2029 to build 564 MW of company-owned natural gas generation for the project.

stories.headline: Russia fires ~70 missiles and 130 drones at Ukraine on Putin's birthday; at least 24 killed

key_facts.fact: Russia struck Kyiv and 12 Ukrainian regions overnight into Oct 7, which coincided with Vladimir Putin's 74th birthday; Zelensky said 70 missiles, many ballistic, were fired along with Shahed drones.
key_facts.excerpt: the October 7 attack included "70 missiles in total, many of them ballistic, as well as Shahed-drones" launched on 12 Ukrainian regions.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 130 drones, 48 cruise missiles and an unspecified number of ballistic missiles; air defences downed 161 targets.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia launched 130 drones, 48 cruise missiles, and an unspecified number of ballistic missiles in the overnight attack. It added air defence units downed 161 targets.

key_facts.fact: A Russian missile destroyed a five-storey apartment building in Pryluky, Chernihiv region; AP reported at least 24 civilians killed nationwide, including four children.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian strikes on Ukrainian cities kill at least 24 in a major attack that Kyiv saw coming

key_facts.fact: Kyiv Independent later tallied at least 28 killed and 134 injured over 24 hours, 18 of them in Pryluky.
key_facts.excerpt: At least 28 people were killed and at least 134 were injured in Russian attacks against Ukraine in the past 24 hours... Eighteen of those killed died when a Russian cruise missile hit a residential building in Pryluky

key_facts.fact: Russia's Defence Ministry said it targeted sites where Fire Point makes and stores Flamingo cruise missiles and long-range drones, plus port and ship-repair infrastructure in Odesa.
key_facts.excerpt: Targets included sites where the company Fire Point makes and stores Flamingo cruise missiles and medium- and long-range drones in Kyiv

key_facts.fact: Ukraine said it hit two oil facilities and a training ground in Russia's Perm, Samara and Astrakhan regions; Russia said naval drones set a Liberian-flagged tanker ablaze near Sochi, with all 23 Indian crew rescued.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia's Transport Ministry said a Liberian-flagged tanker had been attacked by "naval drones" near ... Sochi ... the crew of 23, all Indian citizens, had been rescued

key_facts.fact: Ukraine lacks ammunition for its US-made Patriot systems to stop Russian ballistic missiles; Patriot interceptors are in short supply due to the Iran war.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine is looking worldwide for available Patriot missiles, which are in short supply due to the Iran war.

stories.headline: Vance signals softer US enrichment demand on Iran as Rubio says Tehran lost control of Hormuz

key_facts.fact: In a Reuters interview published Tuesday, VP JD Vance said Iran must make a 'meaningful' cut to its enrichment capacity to end the war, rather than Trump's earlier 'no enrichment' demand.
key_facts.excerpt: Vice President JD Vance appeared to soften U.S. demands on Iran to end the war Tuesday, saying Tehran must do something "meaningful" to reduce their nuclear enrichment

key_facts.fact: Speaking in Athens on Oct 7, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Iran had 'lost complete control' of the Strait of Hormuz and its economy was 'in total and complete freefall'.
key_facts.excerpt: "The Straits of Hormuz are open. There's almost as much oil flowing out now as there was before this conflict began. So they've lost complete control of the Straits," Rubio told reporters during a visit to Athens.

key_facts.fact: IRGC adviser Mohammad Reza Naqdi said 'illegal' routes along Oman's coast would soon be blocked and that the strait remains closed until Iran's demands are met.
key_facts.excerpt: Transit routes in the Strait of Hormuz deemed illegal by Iran will soon be closed, an adviser to the Revolutionary Guards' Commander told the semi-official Fars News Agency on Wednesday

key_facts.fact: Iran's army spokesman said Wednesday the armed forces were prepared to carry out pre-emptive strikes in the war against the US.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's army spokesman said on Wednesday that the armed forces were prepared to carry out pre-emptive strikes in the war against the US

key_facts.fact: On Tuesday 12 crew were injured when a projectile struck the Panama-flagged tanker On Peace in the strait; Oman rescued 10 crew after the vessel caught fire.
key_facts.excerpt: On Tuesday, Oman's defense ministry said in a statement that it rescued 10 crew members from the commercial vessel On Peace, which caught fire after being attacked.

key_facts.fact: The cost of shipping oil from the Persian Gulf to China hit a record $1.3 million a day on Monday, versus close to $60,000 a day on average last year.
key_facts.excerpt: The cost of carrying oil from inside the Persian Gulf to China rose to a record $1.3 million a day Monday, according to data from the Baltic Exchange in London. The rate averaged close to $60,000 a day last year

key_facts.fact: Gulf oil flows excluding Iran reached more than 81% of pre-war levels in September, according to Kpler.
key_facts.excerpt: Gulf oil flows, excluding Iran, reached more than 81 percent of pre-war levels in September, according to maritime intelligence firm Kpler.

stories.headline: S&P 500 closes above 7,800 for first time as 10-year yield eases from 2002 high

key_facts.fact: On Oct 6 the S&P 500 rose 0.58% to a record 7,818.93, its first close above 7,800; the Nasdaq added 0.45% to a record 27,599.79 and the Dow 0.49% to 51,521.28.
key_facts.excerpt: The S&P 500 rose 0.58% to a record 7,818.93 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 0.45% to a record 27,599.79. The Dow added 0.49% to 51,521.28

key_facts.fact: The 10-year Treasury yield fell about 4 basis points to 5.27% after Monday's 5.31% close, the highest since April 2002.
key_facts.excerpt: The 10-year yield fell 0.040 percentage point to 5.270% ... after a two-session climb that had taken it to 5.310% on Monday, the highest close since April 2002.

key_facts.fact: Treasury sold $58 billion of three-year notes at 4.932%, the highest three-year auction yield since May 2006.
key_facts.excerpt: The Treasury sold $58 billion of three-year notes at 1 p.m. at a high yield of 4.932%

key_facts.fact: Futures priced roughly a 20% chance of a Fed rate increase at the Oct 27-28 meeting and about 86% by December; minutes of the September meeting, at which the Fed raised rates, were due Wednesday.

stories.headline: US government, Google DeepMind and Meta join Biohub's $1.8B push to build AI-ready biology data

key_facts.fact: Biohub announced on Oct 7 that the US government, Alphabet and Meta are joining its Virtual Biology Initiative, bringing commitments to $1.8 billion in funding, data, compute and measurement technology.
key_facts.excerpt: Biohub announced on Wednesday that the U.S. government, Google $GOOGL parent Alphabet, and Meta $META are joining its Virtual Biology Initiative, bringing total commitments to $1.8 billion

key_facts.fact: Google DeepMind, Isomorphic Labs and Meta are collectively investing $300 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Google DeepMind, Meta, and AI drug discovery startup Isomorphic Labs are jointly investing $300 million into Biohub

stories.headline: Brussels weighs broad levy on all large companies to tax US Big Tech without a digital tax

key_facts.fact: The European Commission is considering taxing US tech groups such as Apple, Meta and Google through a broad levy on large corporations, to avoid a backlash from the Trump administration, the FT reported on Oct 7 citing six officials.
key_facts.excerpt: Brussels is considering taxing big US tech companies through a broad levy on large corporations in an effort to raise revenues for the EU while avoiding a backlash from the Trump administration

key_facts.fact: The plan would modify the 'Corporate Resource for Europe' (CORE) proposal, which charges every company with more than EUR100 million in EU revenue a fixed annual levy of EUR100,000 to EUR750,000.
key_facts.excerpt: In its current form, CORE requires these companies to pay a fixed annual levy of between €100,000 and €750,000

key_facts.fact: Trump threatened in June a 100% tariff on all goods from any country imposing a digital services tax on US companies.
key_facts.excerpt: US President Donald Trump in June threatened a 100% tariff on all goods from any country that imposes a digital services tax on American companies.

key_facts.fact: CORE is one of five new 'own resources' meant to raise about EUR60bn a year from 2028; a majority of EU states currently oppose CORE and any change needs unanimity of all 27.

stories.headline: South Korea's Nuri rocket deploys five NEONSAT satellites, its fourth straight success

key_facts.fact: Nuri lifted off from the Naro Space Center at 12:25 p.m. local time on Oct 7 (0325 GMT) carrying 15 satellites, South Korea's first orbital launch of 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Liftoff occurred at 11:25 p.m. EDT (0325 GMT and 12:25 p.m. local time on Oct. 7).

key_facts.fact: All five NEONSAT microsatellites (Nos. 2-6), the primary payload for the country's first domestically launched microsatellite constellation, deployed; nine of 10 CubeSats separated, while Quaternion's PERSAT-02 failed to separate.
key_facts.excerpt: The rocket successfully deployed its primary payload of five ... NEONSAT microsatellites, while nine of its 10 CubeSat secondary payloads were released as planned

key_facts.fact: It was Nuri's fifth launch and fourth consecutive success, raising its success rate from 75% to 80%; it was also the first Nuri launch to proceed without delay.
key_facts.excerpt: The mission was Nuri's fifth launch overall and its fourth consecutive success after its maiden flight failed in 2021, raising its overall launch success rate from 75 percent to 80 percent.

key_facts.fact: Each NEONSAT weighs under 100 kg and can resolve objects as small as 1 meter; the full 10-satellite constellation, completed by a sixth Nuri flight in H2 2027, will image the Korean Peninsula more than three times a day.
key_facts.excerpt: Each NEONSAT weighs less than 100 kilograms and carries an electro-optical camera capable of distinguishing objects as small as 1 meter

key_facts.fact: All five NEONSATs made initial ground contact by 5:52 p.m.; the government has added five more Nuri flights through 2032 with 328 billion won ($245.1 million) in extra funding.
key_facts.excerpt: the government has since added five more flights through 2032, backed by an additional 328 billion won ($245.1 million) in funding.

stories.headline: ViiV's long-acting HIV shot Cabenuva beats daily pills in patients with uncontrolled virus

key_facts.fact: ViiV Healthcare, majority owned by GSK, said on Oct 6 that the phase IIIb CROWN study met its primary endpoint: at six months long-acting Cabenuva achieved superior viral suppression versus standard daily oral therapy.
key_facts.excerpt: London, 6 October – ViiV Healthcare ... today announced the phase IIIb CROWN study met its primary endpoint, demonstrating that at six months, long-acting Cabenuva ... achieved superior rates of viral suppression

key_facts.fact: The trial enrolled people with HIV-1 who still had detectable virus despite prior daily oral treatment; the injection is given six times a year.
key_facts.excerpt: people living with HIV-1 who have detectable virus despite a history of daily oral ART can directly initiate CAB + RPV LA, administered six times a year

key_facts.fact: CROWN enrolled about 326 adults and adolescents across eight countries at 85 sites.
key_facts.excerpt: The study enrolled approximately 326 participants, including adults and adolescents, across eight countries at 85 study sites.

key_facts.fact: Use in people with detectable virus is not yet approved; data will be shared with health authorities for regulatory review, with full results at an upcoming scientific meeting.
key_facts.excerpt: Use of CAB + RPV LA in people with detectable viremia is investigational and has not been approved by regulatory authorities. ... Full results are planned for presentation at an upcoming scientific meeting.
